blocks.h1: What This Is / What It Is For

blocks.p: The **Settings** window is where you set up APRS Command and confirm it is ready to operate. It holds every configuration screen the app has — your callsign, connections, GPS, maps, and more — in one place, arranged as a row of tabs.

This chapter covers the window itself: how to open it, the tabs it contains, and how saving works. It then gives the **Readiness** tab full treatment, because that is the tab you check right before an activation to answer one question: __am I good to go?__

callout.label: Receive-first by design
callout.text: Opening Settings and looking around never transmits. APRS Command starts receive-only, and the title bar shows a **TX Disabled** badge. Nothing on any Settings tab puts you on the air until you deliberately enable transmit.

steps: Click **Settings** on the menu bar (it is the first menu, before **View**).
The Settings window opens as its own floating window titled `APRS Command Settings`, with the heading **Settings** and the subtitle `Connection and safety settings`.
Pick a tab along the top and make your changes.
Leave the window open while you work, or close it when you are done — the main map keeps running behind it.

blocks.screenshot: The Settings window floating over the main map, showing the row of tabs across the top with the Readiness tab selected.

blocks.p: The Settings window is separate from the main window, so you can drag it aside and watch the map or the message list while you adjust a setting.
Across the top of the window is a single row of tabs. They appear in this order:

rows: Pre-operation go/no-go checklist (covered in detail below)
GPS source setup and live fix status
Downloading and managing map tiles for offline use
Your radio, TNC, and APRS-IS connection ports
Live status of every configured connection port
Sound-card input and output device selection

callout.label: Sub-tabs
callout.text: The **GPS**, **iGate**, and **Digipeater** tabs each split into their own **Setup** and **Status** sub-tabs. Use **Setup** to change values and **Status** to watch what the feature is actually doing.

blocks.p: There is no single window-wide Save button. Each configuration tab saves itself. On tabs where you edit values — for example **GPS**, **Connections**, **iGate**, **Digipeater**, **Managed Modem**, **Smart Beaconing**, and **Audio** — you will find a **Save** button and, on most, a **Revert** button at the bottom.

bullets: **Save** writes that tab's settings to disk and applies them.
**Revert** throws away your unsaved edits on that tab and reloads the last saved values.
Switching tabs does not save for you — click **Save** on a tab before moving on if you changed something there.

callout.label: Save each tab you change
callout.text: Because each tab saves independently, edits you make on one tab are not saved by clicking **Save** on another. If a change did not stick, check that you clicked **Save** on the correct tab.

blocks.p: The **Readiness** tab is a pre-operation checklist for EmComm activations and exercises. It reads the app's current state and shows, at a glance, whether the key pieces you need before operating are in place. It is described in the app as a `Pre-operation checklist for EmComm activations and exercises.`
You do not enter anything on this tab — it is a live status view. It watches the rest of the app and updates on its own.

blocks.screenshot: The Readiness tab with a green "Ready to operate" summary banner at the top and five check cards below, each with a check-mark or cross icon and a detail line.

blocks.p: At the top is a summary banner. When every check passes it reads **Ready to operate** in green. When any check is failing it reads **Not ready — check items below** in red, telling you to scan the list underneath for the item that is not green.

Below the banner is one card per check. Each card shows a status icon on the left, the check's name, and a short detail line explaining the current state. A green check mark (`✓`) means that item passes; a red cross (`✗`) means it does not.

rows: A real callsign is set (not blank and not `N0CALL`)
Shows your callsign, or `Not set — open Station Setup`
`Connected to` your server, `Connecting…`, or `Disconnected — check Connections settings`
`GPS fix active`, `GPS enabled but no fix yet`, or `GPS not enabled — using manual position`
A beacon went out within the last 30 minutes
`Last beacon:` with the time, or `No beacon sent yet — click Beacon Now`
`Transmit allowed`, or `Exercise mode ON — all transmit inhibited`

callout.label: "Ready" does not mean the app has transmitted on its own
callout.text: The last check, **Exercise mode OFF (transmit allowed)**, turns green only to show that transmit is permitted — it does not send anything. Putting a beacon on the air is still a deliberate action you take (for example, **Beacon Now**). If you want the app to stay strictly receive-only, leaving exercise mode ON is a valid state; that single item will simply read red while everything else can still be green.

blocks.p: The Readiness tab refreshes itself. A line at the bottom right reads `Refreshes automatically every 5 seconds.` As you fix each item — set your callsign, connect APRS-IS, get a GPS fix, send a beacon — its card turns green on the next refresh without any action from you. Watch the summary banner flip to **Ready to operate** once all five pass.

callout.label: Use it as your final pre-flight
callout.text: Open **Settings -> Readiness** right before an activation and glance at the banner. Green means every key piece is in place. Red means one card below is still failing — its detail line tells you exactly what to fix and where to go.

bullets: **Readiness says "Not ready" but I can't tell why.** Scan the cards below the banner for the red `✗`. Its detail line names the problem and often the fix (for example, `Not set — open Station Setup`).
**Callsign check stays red.** It fails while blank or set to the placeholder `N0CALL`. Open the **Station** tab, enter your real callsign, and click **Save**.
**APRS-IS check is red.** The detail line shows `Disconnected` or `Connecting…`. Open the **Connections** tab and confirm the APRS-IS port is configured and connected.

**GPS check is red even though I set a position.** Manual position does not count as a GPS fix. This is expected if you operate from a fixed location; the detail line will read `GPS not enabled — using manual position`.
**Beacon check went from green back to red.** The check only counts a beacon sent within the last 30 minutes. Send another beacon (for example, **Beacon Now**) to make it green again.

**Exercise-mode check is red.** Exercise mode is currently ON, which inhibits all transmit. That is intentional if you are staying receive-only; turn exercise mode off only when you actually intend to allow transmitting.
**A change I made didn't save.** Each tab saves on its own. Return to the tab you edited and click its **Save** button; use **Revert** to discard unsaved edits on that tab.
**I don't see a Save button on a tab.** Status-only tabs (like **Ports**, and the **Status** sub-tabs) have nothing to save — they only display live state.
